The Fiscal Responsibility Act’s SNAP reforms align with necessary accountability measures. Expanding work requirements to include parents with older children and limiting state waivers ensures resources target those truly in need while promoting self-sufficiency. Capping benefit growth to inflation prevents unchecked spending, and shifting partial cost responsibility to states incentivizes fiscal discipline—critical when California’s error rates hit 23.1% in FY2023, wasting $1.3 billion.

These changes correct systemic flaws where lax oversight allowed bloated bureaucracies to prioritize dependency over efficiency. While critics claim hardship, the USDA’s 2025 guidance reinforces that work-ready adults must engage in employment or training—non-negotiable for programs funded by taxpayers.

Real reform demands structural accountability, not perpetual expansion.

The data behind these reforms exposes why tightening standards is not just prudent, but overdue—see the evidence: https://t.co/XqPHLT6pW7
